title: Satisfiability, Validity and Falsifiability
quickIdea: Satisfiable means some interpretation makes the formula true; valid means every interpretation does. The two are related by negation, and neither implies the other.
remember: Satisfiable: at least one model exists. Unsatisfiable (a contradiction): no model exists.
Valid (a tautology): true in every interpretation. Falsifiable: false in at least one interpretation.
Valid is the same as not falsifiable. Unsatisfiable is the same as not satisfiable.
F is valid exactly when not F is unsatisfiable; F is satisfiable exactly when not F is not valid.
A formula can be satisfiable and not valid - the ordinary case - but no formula is both valid and unsatisfiable.
Checking satisfiability means hunting for one true row; checking validity means hunting for one false row. The second is usually faster.

example.prompt: Classify (P -> (Q or R)) -> ((P and Q) -> R).
example.work: At P = true, Q = true, R = false the left side is true -> true = true and the right side is (true) -> false = false, so the formula is false there. At P = Q = R = true it is true.
example.answer: Satisfiable but not valid - it has both a true row and a false row.

gateAngle: GATE 2004 Q.70 is exactly this formula, answered 'satisfiable but not valid' from the single falsifying row. GATE 1991 Q.3(xii) goes the other way: two tautologies force a conjunction to be unsatisfiable.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Is (p -> q) and (q -> p) and (p xor q) satisfiable?
variations.why: (p -> q) and (q -> p) is p <-> q, which is true exactly when p and q agree. p xor q is true exactly when they differ. No row satisfies both, so the conjunction has no model.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: You show that F is not valid. Does that prove not F is satisfiable?
variations.why: Not valid means some interpretation makes F false, and in that same interpretation not F is true. So not F has a model, which is what satisfiable means.

trap.what: Treating 'not valid' as 'contradiction', or reading a single true row as proof of validity.
trap.why: Validity is a statement about all rows and satisfiability about at least one. A formula that is false in one row is not valid even if it is true in seven.
trap.counterexample: The 2004 formula is true at P = Q = R = true, so it is satisfiable, yet it is not valid because of the row P = Q = true, R = false.

check.question: Is a contradiction satisfiable?
check.explanation: A contradiction is false in every interpretation, so it has no model at all. Satisfiability asks for at least one true row.
